summary: Validated cookie-session auth migration and security hardening across backend and frontend: login sets cookies, CSRF enforcement works on state-changing endpoints, bearer compatibility remains, logout clears session, lockout triggers, settings/audit/collector flows remain functional, and executive read flows show no regression.

ui_bugs.issue: After logout, pressing 'Trigger Mock Cycle' shows raw backend error text (401 JSON) directly in the banner.

action_items: Optional UX hardening: replace raw 401 API error banner with friendlier message (e.g., 'Sign in from Settings to trigger collector').
Continue repository split by removing duplicated auth/settings methods still present in backend/app/repository.py to avoid future drift.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/app/repository.py remains >800 lines and still contains duplicate auth/settings/audit methods alongside split repositories; this increases maintenance risk and can cause behavior drift.
Split was started (auth_repository/settings_repository), but legacy overlapping methods remain in OICRepository and should be removed or redirected to a single source of truth.
test_credentials: Read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md and used: admin@badger.local / BadgerPass123!
seed_data_creation: No new seed data created; used existing seeded monitor dataset and persisted settings restored in tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New targeted file /app/backend/tests/test_auth_cookie_session_security.py covers cookie auth, CSRF checks, bearer fallback, logout invalidation, and lockout. One scenario remains intentionally skipped when admin already exists: first-admin password complexity through register-admin path.
rca of the issue: No backend functional failure reproduced. The only observed UI issue is presentation-level: executive page directly surfaces backend error payload strings when unauthorized actions are attempted after logout.
